text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Wednesday.

GERMANY - German Bunds continued to rise, fuelled by market speculation that the Bundesbank may cut its repo rate, currently fixed at 3.00 percent at Thursday's council meeting.The December Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 99.66, up 0.06 from Tuesday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts settled higher, with the December gilt future setting a contract high of 111-17 before running out of steam, but dealers cautioned the market was long and vulnerable to correction in the near term.The December long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 111-00/32, up 08/32 from Tuesday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French bonds ended another bull run day as the December future settled near another contract high on MATIF and French assets outperformed German debt. The December notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 126.54, up 0.40 from Tuesday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian bond futures held to higher levels supported by gains in other bond markets and continued optimism over Italy joining a single European currency, but some caution was creeping in over the passage of the Italian 1997 budget through parliament.The December bond future on LIFFE was trading at 123.70, up 0.42 from Tuesday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - Prices of U.S. Treasury securities were firm near midday, trading in a fairly narrow range after getting a boost overnight. The long bond briefly rose a full half a point earlier in the morning but sank later as rumors of Russian President Boris Yeltsin's demise filtered throught the market. The December Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 111-01/32, up 02/32 from Tuesday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.80 percent.

JAPAN - The key December Japanese Government Bond contract ended Tokyo firmer, but the cash market was easier in late trade, with the long-end of the curve suffering most losses. In after hours trading the December future on LIFFE was trading at 123.46, up 0.36 from Tuesday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - Deals were launched in most mainstream currencies and issue types during another hectic morning in the new issues market. Stagecoach issued a 545 million sterling securitisation of receivables due to Porterbrook, a recent acquisition. GECC set a one-year 2.0 billion Slovak crown bond. The EIB became the latest borrower in zero coupon marks. Deutsche Bank added to its range of ultra long-dated zero coupon bonds with a Danish crown offering. Other activity spanned dollars, French francs, marks, New Zealand dollars, pesetas and Swedish crowns.
